title: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
seo_title: Grade 5 Volume of Rectangular Prisms Worksheets (TEKS 5.6A, 5.6B, STAAR)
standard_text: 5.4G use concrete objects and pictorial models to develop the formulas for the volume of a rectangular prism, including the special form for a cube (V = l x w x h, V = s x s x s, and V = Bh); 5.6A recognize a cube with side length of one unit as a unit cube having one cubic unit of volume and the volume of a three-dimensional figure as the number of unit cubes (n cubic units) needed to fill it with no gaps or overlaps if possible; 5.6B determine the volume of a rectangular prism with whole number side lengths in problems related to the number of layers times the number of unit cubes in the area of the base
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 volume worksheets for Texas TEKS 5.4G, 5.6A and 5.6B: count unit cubes, layers, V = l × w × h and V = Bh, missing edges, two prisms and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: V = l × w × h = B × h.
key_sub: Volume counts unit cubes: the cubes in one layer times the number of layers. Use cubic units.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A unit cube has a volume of 1 cubic unit. Volume is the number of unit cubes that fill a figure with no gaps or overlaps.
  • A rectangular prism is layers: the cubes in the base times the number of layers. V = B × h, where B is the area of the base.
  • V = l × w × h. For a cube, V = s × s × s.
  • Volume is in cubic units: cubic centimeters, cubic feet.

Examples

Example

A box is 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm high.

B = 6 × 4 = 24

V = 24 × 3

Answer: 72 cubic centimeters

Example

A cube has 5-inch edges.

5 × 5 × 5

Answer: 125 cubic inches

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting only the cubes you can seeCount the cubes in one layer, then multiply by the number of layers.
Adding the edgesVolume multiplies: l × w × h.
Writing square unitsVolume is in cubic units.

faq.a: Recognize a unit cube as one cubic unit and the volume of a 3D figure as the number of unit cubes needed to fill it.
Find the volume of a rectangular prism as the number of layers times the number of unit cubes in the area of the base.
Use models to develop the volume formulas V = l × w × h, V = s × s × s and V = Bh.

faq.q: What is B in V = Bh?
faq.a: The area of the base. For a rectangular prism, B = l × w.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cubic unit. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 2 rows of 2 cubes = 4 cubes. There are 2 layers: 4 × 2 = 8 cubic units. Count the cubes you cannot see, too (only 7 cubes show a face).

items.q: The layers of this prism are pulled apart. How many unit cubes are in the whole prism?
items.e: One layer: 5 × 3 = 15 cubes. 3 layers: 15 × 3 = 45 cubes.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cubic unit. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 3 rows of 5 cubes = 15 cubes. There are 2 layers: 15 × 2 = 30 cubic units. Count the cubes you cannot see, too (only 22 cubes show a face).

items.q: The bottom layer of a tray has 6 rows of 5 unit cubes. The tray holds 2 layers. How many unit cubes fill it?
items.e: One layer: 6 × 5 = 30 cubes. 2 layers: 30 × 2 = 60 cubes.

items.e: The bottom layer is 5 cubes across and 4 cubes deep: 5 × 4 = 20 cubes. The front face shows 5 × 2 = 10 cubes, but that is not a layer.

items.e: One layer: 4 × 6 = 24 cubes. 3 layers: 24 × 3 = 72 cubes.

sets.title: Use V = l × w × h and V = B × h

items.q: A cube has edges that are 6 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge of a cube is 6 cm, so V = 6 × 6 × 6 = 36 × 6 = 216 cu cm.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 11 × 7 × 4 = 77 × 4 = 308 cu in. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu in.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 10 × 7 × 7 = 70 × 7 = 490 cu ft. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu ft.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 14 × 6 × 7 = 84 × 7 = 588 cu cm. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu cm.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 15 sq cm. The prism is 12 cm tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h, where B is the area of the base: 15 × 12 = 180 cu cm. Think of 12 layers with 15 cubes in each.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 11 m long. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge of a cube is 11 m, so V = 11 × 11 × 11 = 121 × 11 = 1,331 cu m.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 13 × 3 × 11 = 39 × 11 = 429 cu in. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu in.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 14 × 6 × 10 = 84 × 10 = 840 cu m. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu m.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 14 × 6 × 11 = 84 × 11 = 924 cu m. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu m.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 120 sq in. The prism is 8 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h, where B is the area of the base: 120 × 8 = 960 cu in. Think of 8 layers with 120 cubes in each.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 9 in long. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge of a cube is 9 in, so V = 9 × 9 × 9 = 81 × 9 = 729 cu in.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 9 × 5 × 12 = 45 × 12 = 540 cu in. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu in.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 24 sq in. The prism is 5 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h, where B is the area of the base: 24 × 5 = 120 cu in. Think of 5 layers with 24 cubes in each.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 48 sq m. The prism is 9 m tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h, where B is the area of the base: 48 × 9 = 432 cu m. Think of 9 layers with 48 cubes in each.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 36 sq ft. The prism is 7 ft tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h, where B is the area of the base: 36 × 7 = 252 cu ft. Think of 7 layers with 36 cubes in each.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 6 × 2 × 12 = 12 × 12 = 144 cu cm. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu cm.

items.q: A box is 8 ft long, 5 ft wide and 2 ft tall. Which expression gives its volume?
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 8 × 5 × 2 = 80 cubic feet.

items.q: A box is 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm tall. Which expression gives its volume?
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic centimeters.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 11 × 8 × 7 = 88 × 7 = 616 cu cm. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu cm.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 15 × 5 × 11 = 75 × 11 = 825 cu ft. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu ft.

items.q: A prism has a volume of 336 cu m and a height of 8 m. What is the area of its base?
items.e: V = B × h, so B × 8 = 336. B = 336 ÷ 8 = 42 sq m. Area is in square units.

items.q: A cube has a volume of 64 cu in. How long is each edge?
items.e: All 3 edges of a cube are equal. Find the number that you multiply 3 times to get 64: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64. Each edge is 4 in.

sets.title: Add the volumes of two prisms

items.q: A model building has two parts shaped like rectangular prisms. One part is 12 cm by 9 cm by 7 cm. The other part is 8 cm by 5 cm by 7 cm. What is the total volume?
items.e: First part: 12 × 9 × 7 = 756. Second part: 8 × 5 × 7 = 280. Add: 756 + 280 = 1,036 cu cm.

items.q: A set of concrete steps is made of two rectangular prisms. One part is 8 m by 3 m by 2 m. The other part is 3 m by 3 m by 4 m. What is the total volume?
items.e: First part: 8 × 3 × 2 = 48. Second part: 3 × 3 × 4 = 36. Add: 48 + 36 = 84 cu m.

items.q: Mateo builds a solid from two rectangular prisms. The total volume is 150 cu cm. Prism A has a volume of 90 cu cm. Prism B is 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. How tall is prism B?
items.e: Prism B: 150 − 90 = 60 cu cm. Then 5 × 3 × h = 60, so 15 × h = 60 and h = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 cm.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 12 × 5 × 2 = 120. Prism B: 9 × 5 × 5 = 225. Add: 120 + 225 = 345 cu m. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 5, not 7.

items.q: Harper builds a solid from two rectangular prisms. The total volume is 200 cu in. Prism A has a volume of 120 cu in. Prism B is 4 in long and 5 in wide. How tall is prism B?
items.e: Prism B: 200 − 120 = 80 cu in. Then 4 × 5 × h = 80, so 20 × h = 80 and h = 80 ÷ 20 = 4 in.

items.q: This solid is made of unit cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Bottom prism: 5 × 2 × 1 = 10 cubes. Top prism: 3 × 2 × 2 = 12 cubes. 10 + 12 = 22 cubic units. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 10 × 2 × 5 = 100. Prism B: 6 × 2 × 6 = 72. Add: 100 + 72 = 172 cu ft. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 6, not 11.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 10 × 2 × 6 = 120. Prism B: 6 × 2 × 5 = 60. Add: 120 + 60 = 180 cu m. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 5, not 11.

items.q: This solid is made of unit cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Bottom prism: 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cubes. Top prism: 2 × 3 × 3 = 18 cubes. 30 + 18 = 48 cubic units. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 9 × 5 × 6 = 270. Prism B: 7 × 5 × 5 = 175. Add: 270 + 175 = 445 cu in. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 5, not 11.

items.q: This solid is made of unit cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Bottom prism: 5 × 3 × 3 = 45 cubes. Top prism: 2 × 3 × 1 = 6 cubes. 45 + 6 = 51 cubic units. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: Which expression gives the volume of this solid?
items.e: Prism A: 6 × 2 × 2 = 24. Prism B: 3 × 2 × 4 = 24. Add: 24 + 24 = 48 cu ft. Each prism needs all 3 of its own edges, and B is only 4 ft tall.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 7 × 4 × 3 = 84. Prism B: 5 × 4 × 6 = 120. Add: 84 + 120 = 204 cu ft. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 6, not 9.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 10 × 5 × 3 = 150. Prism B: 6 × 5 × 6 = 180. Add: 150 + 180 = 330 cu in. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 6, not 9.

items.q: Which expression gives the volume of this solid?
items.e: Prism A: 9 × 2 × 5 = 90. Prism B: 3 × 2 × 4 = 24. Add: 90 + 24 = 114 cu cm. Each prism needs all 3 of its own edges, and B is only 4 cm tall.

items.q: This solid is made of unit cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Bottom prism: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cubes. Top prism: 2 × 3 × 1 = 6 cubes. 24 + 6 = 30 cubic units. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: Two wooden blocks are glued together to make a toy. One part is 5 in by 4 in by 3 in. The other part is 2 in by 4 in by 6 in. What is the total volume?
items.e: First part: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60. Second part: 2 × 4 × 6 = 48. Add: 60 + 48 = 108 cu in.

items.q: A storage shed has two parts shaped like rectangular prisms. One part is 10 ft by 6 ft by 4 ft. The other part is 6 ft by 6 ft by 5 ft. What is the total volume?
items.e: First part: 10 × 6 × 4 = 240. Second part: 6 × 6 × 5 = 180. Add: 240 + 180 = 420 cu ft.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 6 × 4 × 5 = 120. Prism B: 3 × 4 × 4 = 48. Add: 120 + 48 = 168 cu cm. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 4, not 9.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 12 × 3 × 3 = 108. Prism B: 9 × 3 × 2 = 54. Add: 108 + 54 = 162 cu cm. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 2, not 5.

items.q: Sofia packs 1-foot cubes into a crate that is 4 feet long, 3 feet wide and 2 feet tall. How many cubes fit?
items.e: One layer: 4 × 3 = 12 cubes. 2 layers: 12 × 2 = 24 cubes, so the crate is 24 cu ft.

items.q: A moving box holds 3,000 cubic inches. It is 20 inches long and 15 inches wide. How tall is it?
Which of these could be the volume of a shoebox?
items.e: A volume is in cubic units, and a shoebox is about 12 in × 7 in × 5 in = 420 cu in. 600 cu ft would be bigger than a closet.

items.q: Each layer of cubes in a box has 15 cubes. The box holds 90 cubes when it is full. How many layers are there?
items.e: Layers × cubes in each layer = total, so ? × 15 = 90. 90 ÷ 15 = 6 layers.

items.q: A garden bed is made of two rectangular prisms. One is 6 ft by 3 ft by 2 ft. The other is 3 ft by 3 ft by 2 ft. How much soil fills the bed?
items.e: 6 × 3 × 2 = 36 and 3 × 3 × 2 = 18. Add the two parts: 36 + 18 = 54 cu ft.

items.q: A shipping container is 40 ft long, 8 ft wide and 8 ft tall. What is its volume?
A cereal box is 8 inches wide, 3 inches deep and 12 inches tall. What is its volume?
A fish tank is 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 25 cm tall. Water fills it to a height of 20 cm. What is the volume of the water?
items.e: Use the height of the water, not the tank: 30 × 20 × 20 = 600 × 20 = 12,000 cu cm.

items.q: A brick is 8 in long, 4 in wide and 2 in tall. What is the total volume of 10 bricks?
items.e: One brick: 8 × 4 × 2 = 64 cu in. Ten bricks: 64 × 10 = 640 cu in.

items.q: A swimming pool is 25 m long and 10 m wide. The water is 2 m deep everywhere. How much water is in the pool?
items.e: V = 25 × 10 × 2 = 250 × 2 = 500 cu m. 250 is only the area of the pool.

items.q: Isabella stacks 3 boxes that are all the same. Each box is 12 in by 10 in by 6 in. What is the total volume of the 3 boxes?
items.e: One box: 12 × 10 × 6 = 720 cu in. Three boxes: 3 × 720 = 2,160 cu in.

items.q: Caleb packs cubes with 2-inch edges into a box that is 8 in long, 6 in wide and 4 in tall. How many cubes fit?
items.e: Along each edge: 8 ÷ 2 = 4, 6 ÷ 2 = 3, 4 ÷ 2 = 2. Cubes: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24. (192 would be 1-inch cubes.)

items.q: Marcus fills a sandbox that is 6 feet long and 5 feet wide with sand 2 feet deep. How many cubic feet of sand does he need?
items.e: V = 6 × 5 × 2 = 30 × 2 = 60 cu ft. The depth of the sand is the height.

items.q: Storage unit A is 10 ft by 10 ft by 8 ft. Storage unit B is 12 ft by 8 ft by 8 ft. Which holds more, and how much more?
items.e: A: 10 × 10 × 8 = 800 cu ft. B: 12 × 8 × 8 = 768 cu ft. 800 − 768 = 32 cu ft. (Adding the edges gives 28 for both, but that is not volume.)

items.q: Ethan's toy chest is 3 ft long, 2 ft wide and 2 ft tall. How much space is inside it?
Liam's aquarium is 20 inches long, 10 inches wide and 12 inches tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 20 × 10 × 12 = 200 × 12 = 2,400 cu in. 200 is only the area of the bottom.

items.q: Box A is 6 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm. Box B is a cube with 5 cm edges. Which has the greater volume?
items.e: A: 6 × 5 × 4 = 120 cu cm. B: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cu cm. B is greater by 125 − 120 = 5 cu cm.

items.q: Carlos fills a sandbox that is 5 ft long, 4 ft wide and 1 ft deep. Sand costs $3 for each cubic foot. How much does the sand cost?
Which unit could be used to measure the volume of a swimming pool?
items.e: Volume is the space inside a solid, so it uses cubic units. Square meters measure area, meters measure length, and kilograms measure mass.

items.q: A box is 4 in long, 3 in wide and 5 in tall. A second box has the same base but is twice as tall. What is the volume of the second box?
items.e: The second box is 4 × 3 × 10 = 120 cu in. Doubling the height doubles the volume: 2 × 60 = 120. (480 would double every edge.)
